basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum, benedixitque eis dicens: Crescite et multiplicamini, et'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum, benedixitque eis dicens: Crescite et multiplicamini, et replete aquas maris, avesque multiplicentur super terram. Et factum est vespere et mane dies quintus. Quod dixit, crescite, et multiplicamini, et replete aquas maris, ad utrumque genus animantium de aquis factorum, hoc est, et ad pisces pertinet, et ad aves, quia sicut pisces omnes non nisi in aquis vivere possunt, ita sunt pleraeque aves quae etsi in terris aliquando requiescunt, fetusque propagant, non tantum de terra, sed de mari vescuntur, marinisque sedibus libentius quam utuntur terrestribus. Quod vero subjungit, avesque multiplicentur super terram, ad utrumque genus avium, hoc est, et earum quae de aquis, et earum quae vescuntur de terra, respicit, quia videlicet etiam illae quae sine aquis vivere nesciunt aves, ita ut multo saepe anni tempore sub profundo aquarum quomodo pisces lateant, nonnunquam egredi super terras solent, maxime cum fetant et nutriunt pullos.
